integrity.anchor_registry_note: The corpus provenance gate verifies each anchor against the file that anchor names and stores no registry-level digest of its own. This digest is recorded so a signature also pins which anchor set was in force.
integrity.verbatim_block_note: The block in section 3 is the file's decoded text with any single trailing newline removed, which is what the markdown fences require. `record_sha256` above is over the raw file bytes and is the digest a signature refers to; this one is over the text as embedded, so a verifier can compare either.

value: Synthetic process record for a synthetic project.

One of the three acceptance criteria is recorded as not met, on purpose. The instance shows a control that correctly refused to let the process fabricate the artifacts that would make it look satisfied.
The second criterion is unexercised rather than met. A control with no instance cannot be called effective and this record does not call it effective.

known_limitations_verbatim.value: Set to the value above because no human has reviewed or approved this record. `automated_review_status` below refers to corpus automation (schema, link, provenance and consistency checks run by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py) and is not a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation.

outcome_record._note: Fields a human or a later process may fill AFTER a signature exists. Empty here; present so the outcome can be captured without editing the generator.

questions_for_human.question: As the project_manager for this supporting record, do you agree that "SUP.10 Change request management: populated process record for Project Northcell" is a correct and complete statement of project planning, schedule, resources, risk?
questions_for_human.why_this_needs_a_human: Correctness of engineering content is not derivable from the repository. The corpus can prove the record is well-formed and internally consistent; it cannot prove the engineering is right.

questions_for_human.question: This record is a synthetic fixture of the hypothetical reference project this corpus also declares. Is anything in it readable as a claim about the real foxBMS 2 product?
questions_for_human.what_in_this_packet_bears_on_it: The record's profile and corpus_boundaries block.
questions_for_human.why_this_needs_a_human: Contamination between the fictional project and the real one is the failure this corpus's whole as_is/synthetic split exists to prevent, and it is a reading failure, not a data error.

questions_for_human.question: For each standards mapping: is the cited clause the right obligation for this work product, and is the status right?
questions_for_human.why_this_needs_a_human: Clause selection is a reading of a standard, not a property of the repository.

questions_for_human.question: `lifecycle_status` is `baselined`. Is that the right status for this revision?
questions_for_human.what_in_this_packet_bears_on_it: lifecycle_status and its note in section 3.
questions_for_human.why_this_needs_a_human: A status is a claim about how far the work has actually got, and no detector measures it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every change record names its trigger, its affected artifacts, the new revisions, the suspect links and the re-verification selection
acceptance_criteria.evidence_of_conformance: The three pre-existing change records validate. This pass did not author a new change record: the six contradictions it found are recorded as findings, because a change record would assert that a change was decided and the decision has not been taken.
acceptance_criteria.how_conformance_is_checked: Validate against change.schema.json and confirm every one of the five blocks is populated.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No baselined record is edited without a change record authorising it
acceptance_criteria.evidence_of_conformance: Not verifiable across the corpus today, because no record has yet been revised above 1 and so no change has been executed. The criterion is real and currently unexercised; recording it as satisfied would be false.
acceptance_criteria.how_conformance_is_checked: Compare a baselined record's revision history against the change records for its id.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A decision is labelled as a synthetic decision and is never presented as a human approval
acceptance_criteria.evidence_of_conformance: All three pre-existing change records carry synthetic_decision labels and the corpus policy records the label format.
acceptance_criteria.how_conformance_is_checked: Confirm every decision field carries a synthetic_decision label naming a fictional role.

accountable_role.independence: The change board may not approve a change whose author is a board member. The board chair is the project manager and the authors are domain roles, so the separation holds structurally; no human board member exists.

record_verbatim.definition: A change request in this corpus is a change record carrying a trigger, an impact analysis, a decision, the new revisions the change would create, the links it makes suspect and the re-verification it requires. The board decides; this process records. A change that would correct a baselined record is handled here and not by the author editing the record, which is why the six findings raised in this pass are findings and not edits.

outputs.output: A change record with the full impact chain
A decision with a named decision maker and a disposition
A re-verification selection naming the measures to re-run
outputs.retention: for the lifetime of the change

performed_instances.decision_or_outcome: The board accepted all six referrals for future change control. No change record was raised, no record was edited and no revision was raised above 1. The distinction matters: a referral is a problem, a change record is a decision, and only the decision can move a baseline.
performed_instances.instance_description: Referral of six baselined-record corrections to the change board rather than editing the records in place.
non_conformances_found: Criterion 1 is not met for this instance, and deliberately: producing six change records here would assert six decisions that have not been taken. The instance is recorded as partially conforming so the shortfall is visible rather than papered over by authoring records that would be fiction.
outputs_produced: Six change referrals, none of which is a change record

signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer, and archive the signed packet outside docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record, and the corpus rule `human_approval_rejected` fails validation on any record whose human_approval_status is not pending, so no tool can manufacture the state.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action.
